subject: Reserved commit & throughput packaging for Borealis — GPU pool proposal
messages:
From: Ava Michaels <ava@borealis.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Borealis Procurement <procurement@borealis.ai>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@borealis.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 14:12:00 -0400
Subject: Reserved commit & throughput packaging for Borealis — GPU pool proposal

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the serving latency and the ability to do canary rollouts. We're trying to move from eval to a production-ready commit but need a concrete sizing + pricing proposal to take to procurement. Below is a condensed workload profile; happy to share the raw traces (attached) if helpful.

Workload summary (month-on-month expected):
- Average steady-state: 12k requests/minute (200 rps)
- Peak bursts: up to 28k requests/minute sustained for 2–4 hours (470 rps)
- Concurrency target (real-time chat sessions): 250 concurrent sessions (each holding a 4k context), typical turn is ~600 tokens output
- Average input + output tokens per request: ~1,200 tokens (context reuse high for repeated sessions)
- Model family: open-llm-65B (we plan to use a quantized 8-bit variant); pref H100-class performance
- SLO: p95 latency <350ms for 512-token responses; p99 <700ms preferred
- Data residency: US only; 12-month term preferred, open to 24-month for better pricing

Ask: Can you propose 2–3 reserved commit options (pool sizes) with expected throughput guarantees, token throughput / GPU estimates, and a pricing + discount ladder for 12- and 24-month commitments? Also confirm whether Redwood can provide automated prefix/KV caching for session reuse (we expect heavy reuse).

I've attached our workload summary export. Planning to present to procurement on Aug 16, so would appreciate an initial proposal by EOD Aug 12.

Thanks,
Ava Michaels
Head of Platform
Borealis Health
[Attachment: borealis_workload_summary.csv (CSV, 24KB)]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Ava Michaels <ava@borealis.ai>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@borealis.ai>, procurement@borealis.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 17:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Reserved commit & throughput packaging for Borealis — GPU pool proposal

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear workload export, that helps a lot. Initial read below (quick answers up front):

- Yes, Redwood supports prefix/KV caching and we can configure session affinity to maximize KV reuse; that materially reduces per-token cost for long-lived sessions.
- I put together three sizing options (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive) with expected throughput and a delta on cost/latency. I attached the pricing summary (PDF) and a brief runbook for autoscaling/fallback.

Key clarifying Qs before finalizing numbers:
1) Expected monthly token volume (approx): do you expect the 1,200 tokens/request * 12k RPM steady-state = ~518M tokens/day or were there other reuse assumptions?
2) Do you need strict p99 latency credits (service credits) for SLA breaches or is a best-effort + runbook ok to start?
3) Any PKI/KMS requirements for the Private deployment path?

High-level sizing (provisional):
- Conservative (cost-first): 8 H100-equivalent GPUs pool. Estimated steady throughput ~180k tokens/sec (with caching), p95 ~380ms for 512-token responses. Good for heavy reuse but limited burst headroom.
- Balanced (recommended): 12 H100-equivalent GPUs. Estimated steady throughput ~270k tokens/sec, comfortable handling your stated peaks with autoscaling to burst pools; p95 ~320ms.
- Aggressive (latency-first, more headroom): 20 H100-equivalent GPUs. Estimated steady throughput ~450k tokens/sec, p95 ~260–300ms and headroom for sustained bursts.

Pricing sketch (per GPU-equivalent / month, list): 12-month prepay: $12,750 / GPU; 24-month prepay: $10,850 / GPU. We can offer an additional volume discount for pools >=16 GPUs. Exact numbers in attached PDF.

I attached: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.pdf (pricing tiers + discount ladder), and borealis_workload_summary.csv (re-uploaded).

I'll coordinate with Marcus (pricing lead) and Ben (solutions eng) internally and get back with a firm offer and proposed SLA language by EOD Aug 12.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:13:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: Reserved commit & throughput packaging for Borealis — GPU pool proposal

Marcus/Ben — forwarding Borealis thread. Key asks: 12k RPM steady, 250 concurrent sessions w/ 4k context, peaks to ~28k RPM for hours. They prefer 12-month commit but are open to 24 months.

Please see my provisional sizing below (copied from my reply):
- Conservative: 8 H100-eq GPUs (cost-first)
- Balanced (rec): 12 H100-eq GPUs
- Aggressive: 20 H100-eq GPUs (latency-first)

Requests:
- Marcus: confirm discount ladder we can offer for 12 vs 24 months and whether we can extend an additional 10% for strategic accounts (requires BD approval) — we should aim to hold a pricing band so procurement can’t push for deeper one-off discounts. Also confirm monthly vs prepaid price points and what credits to include for SLA misses.
- Ben: can you validate the throughput assumptions (tokens/sec per GPU with 4k contexts, KV cache hit assumptions) and the recommended autoscale headroom for 250 concurrent sessions + 2–4 hour sustained peaks? Add notes on migration/runbook for canary + fallback to smaller models if we hit capacity.

I've attached the workload CSV and pricing PDF. Need to send a consolidated offer to Borealis by EOD Aug 12.

Thanks — Priya
[Quoted below]

On Tue, Aug 10, 2027 at 5:08 PM Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Ava — thanks for the clear workload export...

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 11:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved commit & throughput packaging for Borealis — GPU pool proposal

Thanks Priya — quick notes and a recommended commercial package.

Commercials: (final numbers to legal/finance signoff)
- Offer A (12-month, Balanced - recommended): 12 H100-eq GPUs at $11,900 per GPU/month (prepay annual = invoice upfront). 12-month term, 12x GPUs = $170,800/mo equivalent. We will provide a 12% discount on top of list for strategic/partner credits (effective net price ~ $10,472/GPU).
- Offer B (24-month, Preferred by customer): 12 H100-eq GPUs at $10,200 per GPU/month (prepay 24-month = invoice upfront or quarterly), with a 15% strategic discount possibility after BD sign-off.
- Offer C (Aggressive): 20 GPUs, price per GPU steps down 6% beyond 16 GPUs.

SLA / throughput guarantees: recommend including the following clause in the SOW:
- Redwood will target p95 latency <350ms for 512-token responses for the Balanced pool. If p99 latency breaches occur for >3 days in a 30-day window, customer will be eligible for service credits (5–15% of monthly fee depending on severity).
- Throughput guarantee: baseline reserved throughput will be defined as X tokens/sec per H100-eq GPU for your model family (we compute from your traces). We put a 20% autoscale buffer for sustained peaks, and a rapid-burst buffer (best-effort) for transient spikes.

Pricing negotiation guidance:
- Authorize up to 12% standard discount for 12-month prepay offers; anything >12% needs BD exec approval. For 24-month deals, we can go to 15% after BD approval.
- For pools >=16 GPUs, reduce per-GPU price by an additional 6% to reflect allocation efficiency.

Operational notes for Ben: please validate the tokens/sec per GPU assumptions and the KV cache hit rate (I used 45% hit for steady-state). Also confirm whether we should recommend private VPC for Borealis given PHI concerns.

— Marcus
Head of Pricing & Commercials
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>

Subject: Final: Reserved commit proposal & next steps (Borealis)

Hi Ava / procurement team — thanks for the patience while we finalized numbers. Attached is our formal offer (SOW + pricing table) and a short runbook for onboarding. Summary below (Balanced recommendation):

Summary offer (Balanced — recommended):
- Pool: 12 H100-equivalent GPUs (reserved capacity)
- Pricing (12-month prepaid): $11,900 / GPU / month list; 12% strategic discount applied -> effective $10,472 / GPU / month
- Total effective monthly charge: $125,664 (12 GPUs after discount)
- SLA: p95 latency target <350ms for 512-token responses; service credits apply for sustained p99 breaches (5–15% per clause in SOW).
- Autoscaling & caching: 20% buffer for sustained peaks; KV/prefix caching enabled with session affinity.
- Onboarding: 2-week technical onboarding window; canary policy and automated rollback runbook included.

Docs & next steps:
- Attached: SOW + pricing (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.pdf), onboarding runbook
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/987654321
- DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/envelope/ENVELOPE-12345 (I will send the envelope to procurement once you confirm the billing entity / PO number)

If this looks good I’ll route to legal for a standard SOW and send the DocuSign envelope. If you prefer a 24-month term I can re-run the math (we can typically improve the per-GPU price by ~10–12% on a 24-month prepay).

Thanks again — happy to hop on a quick call if procurement has questions.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
